_readme: Maps Teltonika FMC001 (OBD-II plug-in) AVL I/O element IDs → PREDICT sensor types.
Per-model file: the bridge picks avl_map.<model>.json by the IMEI→model mapping in BRIDGE_DEVICES (see fmc_bridge.py). Sibling file: avl_map.fmc150.json.
The bridge publishes value = raw * scale + offset.

kind 'sensor' → payload.sensors[sensor_type]; kind 'meta' → top-level payload field (e.g. ignition, vin); kind 'dtc' → published to teltonika/{imei}/dtc; kind 'event' → published to teltonika/{imei}/event (eco-driving).
encoding 'ascii' → variable-length (8E X-group) bytes are decoded as ASCII instead of hex (needed for AVL 256 VIN and AVL 281 fault codes).
AVL IDs follow the Teltonika wiki page 'FMC001 Teltonika Data Sending Parameters ID' — IDs 30-60 are the standard OBD-II PID group, 256/281/402 require Data Protocol = Codec 8 Extended on the device.
sensor_type strings MUST stay in sync with backend/app/services/provisioning.py (FMC001_SENSOR_CATALOG) and backend/app/db/init_db.py (SEED_RULES).

Not every car answers every OBD PID. Discovery tool: the bridge logs every UNMAPPED AVL ID it receives (check `docker compose logs -f bridge`) so you can see exactly what your car sends and adjust here — NO code changes needed.

io_elements.name: Battery Voltage
io_elements._comment: External (vehicle) voltage, sent in mV → V

io_elements.name: Vehicle Speed
io_elements._comment: Teltonika standard (GNSS-based speed also in gps block)

io_elements.name: Odometer
io_elements._comment: Total odometer, sent in m → km

io_elements.name: VIN
io_elements._comment: 17-char ASCII VIN via 8E X-group — top-level payload field, not a dashboard sensor

io_elements.name: DTC Count
io_elements._comment: Number of active diagnostic trouble codes

io_elements.name: Distance Traveled MIL On
io_elements._comment: Distance driven with the check-engine light on

io_elements.name: Fuel Level
io_elements._comment: OBD fuel level — FMC001 id, differs from FMC150 CAN (81)

io_elements.name: Control Module Voltage
io_elements._comment: ECU supply voltage, multiplier 0.001 — charging-system health

io_elements.name: Fault Codes
io_elements._comment: Comma-separated ASCII codes via 8E X-group — bridge splits and publishes each to teltonika/{imei}/dtc

io_elements.name: Distance Until Service
io_elements._comment: OEM PID (FMC001 supported) — countdown to next scheduled service; not every car answers it

io_elements.name: Green Driving Type
io_elements._comment: 1=harsh accel, 2=harsh brake, 3=harsh corner — enable Eco driving in Configurator

io_elements.name: Overspeeding
io_elements._comment: Device overspeeding event — enable Overspeeding in Configurator
